in_text_mentions: Of the 38 POEMS syndrome patients, 35 (94.6%) had osteosclerotic and 32 (86.5%) had mixed lesions (Fig. 7A). Osteosclerotic lesions were typically scattered, variable in size, and plaque-like (Fig. 8), whereas mixed lesions were pouch-shaped or soup bubble-like with a clear sclerotic margin and were generally larger (Fig. 9). Patients with pure osteolytic lesions accounted for 15.8% (6/38) of cases. Osteosclerotic lesions were the most prevalent type of bone lesions, accounting for 76.9% (764/994) of the total, followed by mixed (22.5%) and osteolytic (0.6%) types (Fig. 7B).

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph (no panel letters; treated as panel A) of a real patient's hand with arrows/box annotations highlighting magnified fingernail views, visibly showing white nail discoloration consistent with leukonychia on multiple nails. The caption explicitly states leukonychia of multiple fingernails, the in-text links Figure 2 to cutaneous hyperpigmentation and leukonychia on exam, and the article is a POEMS syndrome case report, so the disease attribution to poems_syndrome is supported by a disease-focused title plus a specific captioned manifestation. Leukonychia is a recognized but less common POEMS skin manifestation (variant typicality) and is absent from the allowed vocabulary, hence placed in proposed_findings; the in-text also associates Figure 2 with diffuse hyperpigmentation, which is tagged from the vocabulary. Skin of the dorsal hand is visible and adequately lit (medium tone, Fitzpatrick III–IV); no ethnicity or age is stated, and image quality is clear.

panels.rationale: Single fundus-photography figure (both eyes presented together, no panel letters in image or caption) from a disease-focused POEMS syndrome article (primary_disease_keys = poems_syndrome). It is a real human-patient ophthalmic image showing bilateral optic disc swelling at initial assessment, which matches the configured finding poems_syndrome_papilledema (bilateral papilledema), a recognized ocular manifestation of POEMS syndrome. The panel is not a diagram/chart, not a control, not third-party (prior triage third_party=false), and the caption does not name Bartonella neuroretinitis; per rule 3 the disease-focused article title plus the specific captioned manifestation supports POEMS attribution. Confidence is tempered because the article describes a Bartonella henselae neuroretinitis coinfection whose fundus pattern (disc edema with incomplete macular star) can overlap with papilledema, so attribution specifically to POEMS rather than the coinfection is moderately high.

Fluorescein angiography shows optic nerve head leakage, macular arteriolar filling defects, and small retinal arteriolar leakage.

source_variant.figure_caption: Fundus photograph and fundus fluorescein angiography. a Hyperemic and generalized optic disc swelling is observed in the right eye. b An opaque and edematous retina in the posterior pole along with pallid “chalky white” generalized optic disc swelling is demonstrated in the left eye. c Fundus fluorescein angiography showing profound leakage of the optic nerve head in the right eye. d Leakage of the optic nerve head, filling defects in multiple arterioles predominantly in the macular area (area within the dashed lines), and leakage of small retinal arterioles (arrowheads) are observed in the left eye
